questions.question: Define deforestation and explain four reasons why the Amazon rainforest is being cleared.
questions.expected_answer: Deforestation is the cutting down or clearing of forests so that the land can be used for something else. In the Amazon, the biggest cause is cattle ranching, where forest is cut and burned to make grassland for cattle. Other causes are farming crops such as soya beans, logging valuable hardwoods such as mahogany, mining for gold and iron ore, and building roads, dams and towns.

questions.question: Describe four consequences of deforestation.
questions.expected_answer: Animals and plants lose their habitats, and some species may become extinct. Indigenous people lose their land, food and way of life. The thin soil is washed away by heavy rain, causing soil erosion, and the land soon becomes poor. The climate is affected, because fewer trees release less water vapour, so some areas may get less rain, and burning trees releases carbon dioxide, which adds to climate change.

questions.question: Describe what is being done to reduce deforestation in the Amazon.
questions.expected_answer: Brazil uses satellites to watch the forest and spot illegal clearing quickly. Stronger laws, monitoring and protected areas helped bring deforestation down a great deal after about 2004, although the rate has gone up and down since. Large areas are national parks or indigenous reserves, some companies practise sustainable logging and label their wood, some farmers practise agroforestry, and shoppers can choose products from well-managed forests.
